# NOTES: Emmanuel Appadocca; or, Blighted Life (Maxwell Philip, 1854, 2 vols; Gutenberg 75313/75314)

Note: the system/environment text above is not part of the novel. Notes cover the novel only.

## Front matter
- Title page: "Emmanuel Appadocca; or, Blighted Life. A Tale of the Boucaneers. By Maxwell Philip." Epigraph: Euripides (Greek, Φεῦ. ὦ μῆτερ...). "In Two Volumes. Vol. I. London: Charles J. Skeet, 10 King William St., Charing Cross. MDCCCLIV."
- Dedication: to Harry Daniels, Esq., 4 Essex Court, Temple; "first-born of my brains"; "a good and true heart."
- Preface (dated Feb 1854, 4 Elm Court, Temple): written in indignation at American slave-holders' cruelty to slave-children; the hero imagines a high-spirited man picking cotton under "Jimboes"/"Quimboes" on his father's plantation. Machinery based on Boucaneer history; scenes mainly in Trinidad, author's native isle. Author wishes his bones lie on rising ground over the sea beside a deceased beloved.

## VOLUME I

**Ch I.** Gulf of Paria described (between NW Venezuela and Trinidad; outlets Dragon's Mouth (north) and Serpent's Mouth (south)). Morning in March: two skiffs. Fishing-boat: master (mixed-blood mulatto, Spanish-seeming) + two black rowers, one named **Jack Jimmy** (comic, Creole dialect: "Garamighty," "massa," "me tink"). Indian-seeming canoe with 12 paddlers and a steersman. Jack Jimmy fears them; canoe follows; hailed to stop; boat rammed/boarded. Ten Indians leap up. Master draws knife, is struck by a paddle from the steersman (Lorenzo in disguise). Jack Jimmy jumps overboard, is recaptured, pretends death. The steersman, who speaks English, has false beard, rifles, cutlasses—reveals pirates. Orders silence. Uses telescope to survey Port of Spain ships; sets course out to sea at 2 o'clock.

**Ch II.** Canoe travels all day to a black Balahoo schooner at night, ("Black Schooner"): sharp, serpent-like, bare masts, anchored head toward Dragon's Mouth. Password "Scorpion." Sentinel: tall, hairy, red cap, red shirt. Sebastian (officer in gold-embroidered black coat, red cap) greets Lorenzo. Prisoners put in cabin. Deck white-scrubbed; device of death's head over crossed bones everywhere; pikes, axes, grappling irons. Lorenzo, in high command, enters main cabin via bronze skull knocker, ring-passport past sentinels, to black boys (Bembo is the master's boy). The captain: ~25, tall, slender, quadroon-looking, light olive skin, basilisk eyes, aquiline nose, raven locks, crimson silk Moorish jacket, gilt poniard, gold-mounted pistols. Cabin: mahogany carved with volcanoes/cataracts in gold and silver, zodiac ceiling, gold-trimmed sea-shell ottomans, globes, gigantic telescope. Books: Bacon's Novum Organum, Aristotle. Lorenzo reports ships in harbour (Letitia of Bristol sugar ship near banks of Caroni). Captain orders five men with fisherman to watch the Dragon's Mouth passage. Gong sounded.

**Ch III.** Revelry: Spanish, Llanero, Frenchman, English songs. Old sailor **Jim Splice** tells tale of buccaneer "Llononois" (commodore) torturing Spaniard for money at Maracaibo, tearing out heart. Jack Jimmy sits at mainmast; sailors pull him up, make him dance, blanket him in a sail; he fakes death; a sailor burns his great toe with a cigar; he revives ("Gad, Lard!"). Fife signals end of revelry. Captain's authority described. Lorenzo reports: large ship passed Boca del Drago.

**Ch IV.** Report on the ship Letitia (stern marked "Letitia" of Bristol, passengers aboard); Lorenzo's sardonic triumph; captain: "Letitia, that is the name: he goes in it. Speed well my purpose!" Captain (in black with gold stripes, red cap with death's head) orders weigh. Passage through the Bocas described. Captain's speech: "Associates... revenge yourselves on the world..." Attack at dawn. Two boats; first boat destroyed by a loaded gun (nails, iron). Second boat boards; the captain's schooner fires; periagua. Captain (Lorenzo's superior) boards; the ship's commander killed by captain's poniard. Captain halts slaughter: "Enough: spare and secure your prisoners." Cut halliards. Cabin: Passenger man of middle age with musket (James Willmington, later named), young lady swooning (Agnes), aged priest. Willmington recognizes captain's voice: "it is my son." Captain: "I am, indeed, your son!" Captain assures Agnes of her honor. Steward hides in pantry, gives papers; ship bound for St. Thomas. Gold in trunks. Pirates cheer. Captain sends Willmington to close custody.

**Ch V.** Morning: 300+ crew in holiday dress. Captain (seated on deck-stool, boys bringing money bags) divides 6,500 dollars; wounded get extra (amputee ×4, eye/finger/toe ×2). Friends of dead claim shares ("Diego," "Martin," "Francis"). Two claim to be Francis's friend; captain orders them to duel ("choose your weapons—at six o'clock"). English sailors of prize (5 of 35 survived; wages £3/month; half advance) paid, released at nearest headland. Master fisherman gets a purse. Jack Jimmy recognizes captain as "my young massa," clasps knees ("you no ’member Jack Jimmy in de mule-pen"); captain says yes and has him led away. Priest and Agnes presented: Agnes described (middle age/young, slender, clear white-olive complexion, dark brown hair, gazelle eyes); Lorenzo attentive. Willmington sentenced: "Prepare, to-morrow, for your trial."

**Ch VI.** Revelry; Jim Splice talks about the captain's discipline. Duel: first claimant stabs second's arm-cloth, then slashes; second kills with poniard in the neck. Wounded man confesses he was not Francis's friend. Lorenzo reports to captain; sentence "Let the punishment be executed upon him." Lots drawn for executioners. Culprit weighted with cannonballs, thrown overboard.

**Ch VII.** Morning trial of Willmington. Captain: "James Willmington... I accuse you of having violated... the law of nature... abandoned your offspring." Long speech ("tiger... bird... serpent" comparison; "I give you ten minutes"). Willmington's defenses: "men are not punished in society for such offences"; "by the laws of the land." Captain: "Look up there... the black flag... no law... save mine and great Nature's." Sentence: cast adrift on a cask with biscuits, "In two hour's time."

**Ch VIII.** Machine built: cask with lead keel, saddle-seat, shelf for biscuits. Willmington pleads, bound, strapped astride cask, lowered from tackles. Priest begs mercy; captain: "I never change." Cask floats away; cries fade. Captain makes sail, turns away. Narrator's aside to reader on callous filial sufferings.

**Ch IX.** Lorenzo at night, writes letter to Agnes; goes to Agnes's passage (forbidden without ring); sentinel nearly discovers him in passage; hides in José's cabin; slips letter under Agnes's door.

**Ch X.** Agnes finds letter next morning: "Lady, though I am a pirate, recoil not from me... I have dared to love you... LORENZO." Agnes weeps; her love "alighted" on Lorenzo. Priest says they'll be landed. Lorenzo, proud and shy, avoids her eyes. Captain reads Lorenzo's love; examines Agnes. Captain instructs master fisherman (given pistols, purse) to protect Agnes, swear "by God and the Holy Virgin"; landing at Granada in three days; "I never forget to punish." Lorenzo tries to speak to Agnes; captain calls "Lorenzo." Jack Jimmy refuses to leave, clasps captain's knees, is allowed to remain. Cutter sets off toward land.

**Ch XI.** Schooner sails on for two days. Third morning St. Thomas sighted. Captain goes ashore in plain clothes, disguised with a panama hat, with Jack Jimmy along. Prize ship is in St. Thomas harbour (Danish port, "Tyre of the West Indies"). Young merchant offers 50, then 55 dollars per hogshead; captain takes 60 in gold (3,600 dubloons). Captain and merchant talk about pirate "Black Schooner." Willmington enters with marines (under a British officer) and a Danish civil official; accuses the captain: "That is he—the pirate." Officer doubts (captain looks too young). Captain goes voluntarily ("If you will take the word of a pirate"). Taken to British man-of-war; commander (venerable old gentleman, rosy, loyal) hears Willmington's account (sloop rescued him; he had the pirate arrested). Captain: "Then you are this gentleman's son?" "Appadocca" is named; Mr. Charles (commander's son, Charles Hamilton) recognizes him: "Appadocca... Emmanuel Appadocca... I studied mathematics with him in Paris." Commander: "Hum."

**Ch XII.** Appadocca locked in a gun-deck compartment; draws algebra on partition with chalk. Night: friend Charles Hamilton visits. Appadocca narrates backstory: studied in Paris for professorship of astronomy (concours). Mother died (letter from her servant); he fell ill. Mother's casket revealed father alive; father is wealthy planter in Trinidad. Appadocca in London: essays rejected; sold telescope for rent (landlord refused to return it); wrote to father asking for help; no answer. On London Bridge, saved a woman (fallen, child) from suicide; gave shoe buckles; reasoned about cosmic law and retribution (lengthy speech). Vow: to visit on his father the same suffering. Went to London Docks, shipped to Jamaica (faking navigation skills by flattery).

**Ch XIII.** Appadocca continues: to San Domingo; exiles living in boucans (huts) as hunters; formed a band of French aristocrat exiles; became captain. Sailed to Trinidad; learned father would sail to England; captured the ship; had him cast adrift on cask. Hamilton urges him to cease; Appadocca renews vow. Lengthy philosophy of social injustice ("in generalibus latet fraus"; "The world... a vast marsh"); commerce vs. mind. Hamilton offers escape ("This very night you will be put on shore"); Appadocca refuses; Hamilton storms out, gives until morning.

**Ch XIV.** Jack Jimmy, after capture, learned from talkers on beach (the man-of-war). Ran two hours; launched a fisherman's canoe; paddled out; met schooner next morning. Tells Lorenzo: "Massa... big English ship, take massa." Lorenzo spies on ship at St. Thomas, sends disguised men to bribe sailors for information.

**Ch XV.** Charles offers escape again; Appadocca still refuses ("What is death?"); talk on transition and death. Noise: men with chisels on dead-light; Lorenzo and crew (greased boat, black caps) cutting; a shark bites line; alarm; flight; Lorenzo shouts "Cowards!" Commander reports marks; orders weigh at dawn. END OF VOL. I.

## VOLUME II

**Ch XVI.** Cutter carrying Agnes and captives to land; becalmed/tacking; Agnes gazes at vanished schooner. Priest's talk on sea's depth/wrecks. Master fisherman stops talk; sailors of captured ship (Bill, others) mutiny, insult the Spaniard; master fisherman shoots two (one dies/fall, one into water, boom knocks a third overboard). Priest makes him stop; ties remaining sailor. Priest decides for Trinidad. Master fisherman steers two days. Agnes reunited with aged father on plantation.

**Ch XVII.** Man-of-war (commander, son Charles, Mr. Cypher, old sailor Jack Gangway, young midshipman) sights Black Schooner, chases it; schooner mocks it; comments. Next day schooner disguised as Mexican brig then brigantine ("Au revoir"). Man-of-war fires; signals exchanged ("You are too far, your guns don't carry"). Pirate flag. Derelict barque "Sting" (Pernambuco to Liverpool, cayenne pepper, English ensign upside-down) found; midshipman boards; schooner transforms out of barque, escapes.

**Ch XVIII.** Lorenzo deceives man-of-war; schooner back in brig rig; Jim Splice seizes midshipman. Midshipman refuses to speak; tortured in spiked box ("torture-room", bows). Revealed: captain is alive, to be taken to Trinidad for trial; schooner sails. Lorenzo gives orders.

**Ch XIX.** Commander rages; orders course to Trinidad. Appadocca brought before commander; refuses to name harbour; offers to communicate via four flags. Signals sent by Appadocca; distant guns fire (signal). Man-of-war sails through Dragon's Mouth; Appadocca, in cabin, breaks port-hole framework; cuts lashings of stool with broken basin pieces; escapes via pitcher ("Now, farewell, good ship") into sea. Sailors think it "slack of the main-brace."

**Ch XX.** Appadocca swims with a clay pitcher; pitcher dissolves; he nearly drowns; rock; sea rising; swept ashore. Llaneros (Juancito) capture him with bull and lassos; carried to Ranchero's house. Ranchero (names: Ranchero, daughter **Feliciana**). Feliciana sees him.

**Ch XXI.** Fever; Feliciana nurses him. Feliciana's passion; she begs him to renounce piracy; he refuses ("My vow is recorded in heaven"). Feliciana vows to follow him. He resolves to leave; he confesses his love-denial, pride.

**Ch XXII.** Appadocca leaves at night by wind direction (wet finger); beach; kills jaguar with bare hands, eats raw flesh. Found by a fallucha (Spanish fishing boat) after waving jacket. Captain of fallucha questions him. Lorenzo's boats meet fallucha at Chaguaramas Bay; Appadocca takes over fallucha ("Submit, I am Appadocca, the young pirate"); finds the Black Schooner hidden.

**Ch XXIII (first).** Schooner's mirror/telescope apparatus (steel poles, mirror globes with white liquid). Lorenzo watches man-of-war; schooner signals "TREAT WELL THE OFFICER, FOR THEY TREAT ME WELL.—SCORPION." Schooner fires guns in reply. Appadocca returns; Jack Jimmy stands on tiptoe; "Thanks to you, Lorenzo"; wine.

**Ch XXIII (second, duplicate number).** Feliciana at Rancha; discovers his absence; leaves; catches sight of fallucha; meets two horsemen (cattle merchants); pays for passage to Guiria.

**Ch XXIV.** Man-of-war at Port-of-Spain. Hamilton urges Willmington to drop prosecution; Willmington refuses; Hamilton insults him ("send him to me"). Servant reports pirate prisoner drowned himself (skylight open). Hamilton grieved. Commander has Willmington landed; Willmington bids commander goodbye. Willmington at Saint Ann's road house; wife (Mrs. Willmington); children.

**Ch XXV.** Willmington's account to family (son, ~18, officer uniform; two infant daughters). Appadocca appears ("Ay, and he never slumbers"). Willmington terrified, pleads. Appadocca: "Make your will." Son attacks with sword; disarmed twice; Appadocca offers duel; son refuses. Appadocca reveals family mark (little finger). Appadocca gags and binds son; Jack Jimmy and Pedro loot silver and gold. Willmington carried off by pirates on pikes. Appadocca's speech to children.

**Ch XXVI.** Two women climb La Vantille hills to hut of Mother Celeste (sorceress; dog Fidele). Feliciana (disguised) asks about her lover; sorceress: "Seek your lover, amidst the tombstones to-morrow." Feliciana despairs.

**Ch XXVII.** Appadocca visits mother's grave in cemetery at Port-of-Spain (plain cross, bamboos). Feliciana finds him there; begs him to renounce vengeance; he refuses. Gives her a lock of hair. Soldiers approach; pirates escape by boat at dawn; soldiers fire.

**Ch XXVIII.** Mrs. Willmington frees servants (Jack the cook, Jim, Bekky); son identifies "brother." Man-of-war gives chase.

**Ch XXIX.** Appadocca releases midshipman; letter to Hamilton (N.B.: tempest warning). Schooner sails for the Serpent's Mouth; hurricane; schooner dashed onto rocks of Trinidad. Willmington's shrieks from torture-room; schooner breaks and he sinks. Appadocca sighs.

**Ch XXX.** Appadocca's philosophy on destiny and honour with Lorenzo; leaves Lorenzo his sword; leaps off rock into the waves; drowned. Jack Jimmy buries his body beneath a grave on beach; Feliciana arrives, learns his name, goes mad.

**Ch XXXI.** Lorenzo lives on island. Meets priest (who blesses); goes to planter (Agnes's father, old cavalier, descended from Carmontes). Lorenzo's real name: St. James Carmonte. Lorenzo marries Agnes. Jack Jimmy serves faithfully, aged. Feliciana becomes "Succouring Mother" in Venezuela, visits Appadocca's grave yearly, tends sea-grape tree. THE END.
